newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEEKS INSOLVENCY FOR TWO BANKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEEKS INSOLVENCY FOR TWO BANKS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) decided on Friday to seek bankruptcy procedures through the courts against private Elitbank and Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC), a BNB official said.
"The BNB board decided to seek the two banks's bankruptcy after it ascertained their insolvency," the official told Reuters.
The decision has yet to be announced officially by the BNB later on Friday.

The decision was in line with International Monetary Fund's (IMF) requirement of closing down insolvent banks as part of restructuring of the crumbling financial sector ahead of planned introduction of a tough fixed exchange rate regime, said the official.

Elitbank was placed in receivership by the BNB on September 23 along with eight other banks due to a capital-to-risk assets ratio of minus 2.42 percent, below Basle banking standard of eight percent, and outstanding payments of 261 million levs.
The BAC has been under severe restrictions since March 1996 when the BNB acquired a 52 percent in it for free to guarantee depositors' savings.
The BNB has sought insolvency for a total of 15 local banks or one third of Bulgaria's banks since May 31, including Elitbank and BAC, but there has been no final court ruling on any of them so far.
Outgoing Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov urged officials to amend legislation to speed up bankruptcy procedures to prevent further erosion of confidence in the banking system.

In November the IMF proposed setting up a currency board system as a last resort to save the crumbling economy from collapse but negotiations on its introduction had been delayed until a new government is in place.
Under the currency board system local currency in circulation must be matched by the amount of foreign currency reserves.

Some $1 billion were withdrawn from commercial banks last year as panicked depositors rushed to convert savings into dollars. Further $1.5 are kept outside banks by the population as matress money, unofficial estimates show.
The lev hit a new historic low of 940 per dollar on Friday from around 600 at the beginning of the year. It traded near 70 a year earlier.
BNB forex reserves fell to $518 million at end-December, down from $1.236 billion a year earlier.
